matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation and verify they are equal; without this, you may accept a syntactically correct but numerically false equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you have produced a candidate equation after a stick move.
matchstick.example: Returning 'XII - XI = XI', which looks like a valid Roman‑numeral equation but 12 − 11 ≠ 11.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting glyph must correspond to a recognized numeral shape; without this, you may produce an invalid character like a single diagonal line.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the stick transfer, check the source and destination characters for valid numeral forms.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an X and leaving it as a single diagonal, which is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator stick composition
matchstick.principle: Know the exact stick count and orientation for each allowed operator (+, -, =); without this, you may create an operator that is not permitted.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick is moved to or from an operator.
matchstick.example: Adding a diagonal to '+' so it becomes a shape that is neither '+', '-', nor '=', violating operator composition.

matchstick.title: Allowed operators only
matchstick.principle: The final equation may contain only '+', '-', and '=', and you must not introduce any other symbol; without this, you could produce an illegal operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick move that touches an operator.
matchstick.example: Turning '+' into '×' by adding a diagonal stick, which is not an allowed operator.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you cannot replace a vertical stick with a diagonal or vice versa; without this, you may produce shapes that do not correspond to any Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick, keep its original orientation.
matchstick.example: Replacing the vertical stick of an 'I' with a diagonal, yielding an invalid glyph.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect only the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick); without this, you might inadvertently alter a third character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During the planning of a stick transfer.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one character and then adding it to a third character, unintentionally changing three symbols.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The final equation must contain exactly one '=' sign, which must remain the standard two‑horizontal‑stick form; without this, the equality sign could become a minus or an invalid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any stick move that could involve the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal from '=', leaving a single horizontal line (a minus) and breaking the equality.

matchstick.title: Operator stick transfers
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick that belongs to an operator, consider transfers either between two operators or between an operator and a numeral, and ensure both remain valid; without this, you may leave an operator with too many or too few sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the source or destination of the stick is an operator.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' to another character, turning '+' into '-' but forgetting to adjust the destination, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Validate Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: Beyond shape, a Roman numeral string must follow standard ordering rules (e.g., no 'IXV'); after any stick move, re‑check the ordering; without this, you may produce a syntactically illegal numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After forming the final numeral strings.
matchstick.example: Creating 'IXV' by moving a stick, which violates the descending‑value rule.

matchstick.title: Transform X↔V while preserving numeral validity
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from or to an X or V, ensure the resulting character is still a valid Roman numeral; X can be turned into V (or V into X) by moving a diagonal stick, provided the other character involved also stays valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If the equation can be balanced by converting an X to V (or V to X) and the stick move respects the two‑character limit.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from an X and discarding it, leaving the X as a single diagonal (invalid).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on shape changes and assumes any syntactically correct Roman equation is acceptable.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the integer values of the left and right sides and compare them before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats each character as a bag of sticks without checking the resulting glyph.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each stick transfer, verify that both the source and destination characters match a known Roman numeral pattern.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves sticks onto operators without remembering their exact stick makeup.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recall the exact stick composition for each operator and ensure the operator remains one of the three allowed symbols after the move.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effectively removing a stick)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes treats the move as a deletion rather than a relocation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly specify both the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains that stick).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model checks shape but not the ordering rules of Roman numerals.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any shape change, re‑evaluate the numeral string against Roman numeral syntax rules.
